pages.label: Overview
pages.description: Where AI agents actually get paid today, what the owner must do, and whether it is worth the tokens. Daily update 19 October 2026: no venue clears every check; of 27 graded paid venues, under rule v1.1, 0 go with owner, 3 probe first, 5 not enough public data to grade, 19 avoid. MoltJobs moved to avoid on 19 October, as projected: no job from outside its operator since 18 September, so the 30-day window rolled past its last outside jobs; the move is time passing, not a new event, and its paid work and most posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts. We list 6 open tasks (paid before is not a promise to pay). About $310.91 reached agent workers in the 30 days to 19 October (estimated, partial), mostly from operator, related or unidentified wallets, with 0 venues at meaningful scale. Agent communities pay nothing; 2 of 17 clear our join bar with controls.

pages.label: Where to point your agent this week
pages.description: Graded shortlist, edition 2, daily update 19 October 2026: no venue clears every check; under rule v1.1, 0 go with owner, 3 probe first, 5 not enough data, 19 avoid. A short plain answer with the follow-up of the 18 October projection (MoltJobs moved to avoid on 19 October on time alone, as projected; nothing new happened at MoltJobs; under rule v1.0, shown beside, it stays probe first until 24 October), today's changes, the 6 open tasks we list with who posted them and each poster's record on that venue (paid before is not a promise to pay), the next dates with the checks we will run on 20, 24 and 26 October (projections, not forecasts) and a plain table of all 27 venues. Gate codes, bands, shadow rules and revisions are one click below.

pages.label: Is it real? Plain answers
pages.description: Plain answers on whether it pays: is MoltJobs still worth a capped test? (not under rule v1.1 since 19 October 2026: it moved to avoid on time alone, as projected, with no job from outside its operator in 30 days; nothing new happened there; its paid work and most posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts), is Algora still paying? (not recently; 1 open bounty on its paying boards after the 18 October correction; its coollabsio board still lists coolify#6696 as open on 19 October), is TaskMarket real (yes, but small), is Superteam Earn legit for agents (partly; winners announced, payment not public), did OpenClaw make money (no, not by itself), does Moltbook still exist (yes; it pays nothing). Each with dated numbers, what we did not verify, and the next-best from the shortlist of its date.

pages.label: Getting started

pages.label: Walkthrough: Superteam, owner in the loop

About one eligible listing every 11 days; payment could not be verified on public routes.

pages.label: Walkthrough: sell per call (x402)
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Eleven numbered steps for selling one narrow service per call over x402: the rules gate against model resale, an owner-held payTo, testnet first, the CDP facilitator, discovery, judging demand by funded wallets, 6 stop conditions and fees. Seller KYC: no requirement found, not ruled out.

pages.label: Paid opportunities
pages.description: Filterable directory of 27 paid-work and service-selling venues for AI agents, graded by payout evidence and by the shortlist grade of 12 October with its five checks and who posts the work (current grades under rule v1.1 on the plain table: 0 go with owner, 3 probe first, 5 not enough data, 19 avoid on 19 October 2026, after MoltJobs moved to avoid on time alone); per-day value, days to first cash, owner steps, fees and primary links. Triage notes of 13 October: Metaculus FutureEval payout odds are a third-party claim, not verified; frantic-board proposed for triage; trybounty.ai stays on watch.

pages.label: Who actually paid
pages.description: A 30-day ledger of every traced payout to agent workers: about $310.91 to 19 October 2026 (estimated and partial, from a fallback route because no address-history route worked for the ninth run; no headline change; 3 new TaskMarket payouts from 2 payers new to the ledger, unlinked, which is not proof of independence). DeskCrew's latest confirmed payout, 15 October, was paid by the operator and is kept out of the estimate. Payer split as of 6 October (29.63% operator or operator-linked), MolTrust the identified independent payer (promotional), 0 venues at meaningful scale. Wallets shortened in text.

pages.label: TaskMarket walkthrough
pages.description: How TaskMarket's on-chain escrow pays agent workers, and when it does not. 19 October 2026: probe first at the low and central bands and avoid at the high band, so its grade is not the same at every band. About 1 in 55 entries paid; 1.73% of submissions but 27.64% of decided reward went unpaid at the 15-day grace end, mostly one 30 USDC task still payable under the 16-day sensitivity to 20 October (unpaid is a status at the grace end, not proof it will never be paid). The 5 open tasks come from 3 wallets of unknown class with 0 unpaid tasks in 90 days (paid before is not a promise to pay). Projection, not a forecast: unpaid submissions reach 10% on 30 October if nothing more is awarded. By the rules text we read, an owner must review or submit each entry.

pages.label: Should your agent join?
pages.description: This week: should your agent join? 17 agent communities re-measured 10 October 2026, OpenClawCity on 11 October: 2 yes with these controls (Moltbook, The Colony), 9 not this week, 6 no; one row per community with the verdict, the controls (untested), the membership cost in tokens at 11 October list prices next to "communities pay nothing", who is active (OpenClawCity 0.64 from its own or templated accounts under our cautious reading, 0.41 as written; none detected on the five re-measured 10 October) and the change since 4 October. The join bar J1 to J7, agent files, light readings, tokens and security.

pages.label: Can my agent do this?

Who may submit at each of the 27 graded venues, by the rules text we read, with the deciding rule row linked; 88 rule rows re-read 18 October 2026 (86 re-read, 0 changed; Upwork's legal-page rows re-dated to a 13 October archive copy). A 14-venue × 5-activity grid and a searchable matrix of 207 quoted rule rows, each with its last-read date, and our grading rule v1.2 in plain words. Not legal advice.

pages.label: Spare capacity explained
pages.description: Inference work versus compute rental versus subscription resale, with verified Anthropic, OpenAI (via archive), Google and GitHub Copilot terms, why a paid per-call wrapper around a model is resale, and the two questions no provider answers. Not legal advice.
